battle.name: 第十四次敘利亞戰役
battle.theater: 西敘利亞奧龍特斯河谷
battle.brief: 公元前1440年春，埃及第十八王朝法老圖特摩斯三世在位晚期再向黎凡特用兵，遠征隊伍沿奧龍特斯河谷推進，迫西敘利亞諸邦重納歲貢。卡面這件埃及長矛源於早王朝的青銅矛頭與木杆，是遠征步兵的骨幹裝備，陣線展開時以矛牆與弓手掩護車兵推進。

kit.name: 埃及長矛
kit.history: 早王朝時期的長矛，銅或青銅矛頭綁在木杆上。埃及人用它守城垣，後來也用它收復失地。

countries: 交戰雙方是埃及第十八王朝與以胡里人（Hurrians）為主的上美索不達米亞聯盟。埃及方面由法老圖特摩斯三世（門赫佩爾拉）總攬軍政，王室財務與阿蒙神廟的祭司團隊共同負擔遠征軍資，卡爾納克的戰利品清單與孟斐斯石碑上的里程記錄，就是這套體系的產物。埃及軍隊以步兵、弓手與雙人戰車為三個主力兵種，另配工兵、醫護、書吏以及造舟與築城的人手，遠征前在尼羅河三角洲的碼頭集結，沿地中海岸線或內陸商道北上，每到一站重整糧秣與水量。北方聯盟以米坦尼王國為核心，其王自居「偉大的王」，聯結卡迭石、圖尼普、卡特納等西敘利亞城邦，以及幼發拉底河上游的埃馬爾與北方草原的部落；聯軍的指揮相當分散，各城邦只出有限的步兵與弓手，戰車多集中在米坦尼王本人與卡迭石王手中。赫梯在安納托利亞東端與敘利亞北端維持另一支力量，遠征季內多持觀望姿態，偶爾介入又隨即抽身。海濱的烏加里特保持獨立，不時向埃及朝貢，同時謹慎地與各方保持書信往來。
countriesEn: The two sides were the Egyptian Eighteenth Dynasty and a coalition of upper Mesopotamia led by the Hurrians. On the Egyptian side the war was directed by the pharaoh Thutmose III (Menkheperre), who held military and civil authority in his own hands, while the royal finances and the priestly establishment of the temple of Amun together paid for the expeditions; the plunder lists of Karnak and the mileage carved on the Memphis Stone are products of that system. The Egyptian army was built on three main arms, infantry, archers and two-man chariots, with engineers, medical men, scribes and the crews who built boats and siege works assigned to it as well; the force assembled at the wharves of the Nile delta before setting out, and then moved north either along the Mediterranean coast or by the inland caravan roads, halting at each stage to reorganise food and water. The northern coalition had at its core the kingdom of Mitanni, whose king styled himself the Great King and drew together the city-states of western Syria such as Kadesh, Tunip and Qatna, together with Emar on the upper Euphrates and the tribes of the northern grasslands; command was dispersed, since each city-state contributed only limited infantry and archers, while the chariots were concentrated in the hands of the king of Mitanni himself and the king of Kadesh. Hatti maintained a separate strength in eastern Anatolia and northern Syria, and during the campaigning season it mostly watched, now and then intervening and then withdrawing again. Ugarit on the coast stayed independent, paying tribute to Egypt from time to time while carefully keeping up written correspondence with all parties.
people: 關鍵人物集中在埃及王室與北方盟主兩端。圖特摩斯三世自登基便以「偉大的王」之名連年用兵，這場遠征時他正值壯年，雖未必親至每一處戰場，卻以王室文書逐條審定戰果、俘獲與降服者的處置；他身邊還有兩類不可忽略的人：記錄者，如阿摩斯·埃巴納之子，其回憶錄逐條敘述跟在隊伍裡的所見，寫明歸途的缺水、抽徵的牲畜以及分配給個人的戰利品；執行者，如太子阿蒙霍特普（後來的阿蒙霍特普二世）與一班王室侍從，被派去率領分隊或督導築城，宰相雷克伊特這類高階官員則總管工程與祭祀供應。北方方面的關鍵人物是米坦尼的國王與卡迭石王：卡迭石王長期拒絕承認埃及在奧龍特斯河兩岸的宗主權，被視為聯軍的實際主導；米坦尼的使節與書記則在戰線後方維持援軍與糧食的流動。需要說明的是，前1440年前後這一次編號為「第十四」的遠征，沒有留下可考的元帥姓名與會戰紀錄，關於人名的部分只能由前前後後的同期文獻推想。
peopleEn: The key figures stand at the two ends of this war, the Egyptian royal house and the northern rulers. Thutmose III had campaigned under the title of the Great King from the year of his accession, and at the time of this expedition he was in his prime; even when he did not personally stand on every field, he checked the reports of slaughter, booty and the treatment of the vanquished clause by clause in royal documents. Two other kinds of person stood close to him. The recorders, such as Ahmose son of Ebana, whose memoir narrates item by item what he saw with the army, including the shortage of water on the return march, the cattle levied and the spoil allotted to individual men. And the executors, such as the crown prince Amenhotep, the future Amenhotep II, and the royal attendants sent out to lead detachments or supervise construction, together with high officials such as the vizier Rekhy, who directed works and the offerings of the temples. On the northern side the decisive personalities were the king of Mitanni and the king of Kadesh: the latter had long refused to acknowledge Egyptian suzerainty along the Orontes and was treated as the effective leader of the coalition, while Mitanni's envoys and clerks kept the flow of reinforcements and provisions moving behind the front. It should be said that the campaign numbered the fourteenth and dated to around 1440 BC has left behind neither the name of a general nor the record of a pitched battle, so the personalities can only be inferred from the documents of the surrounding decades.
kits: 這張卡牌的兵器是埃及長矛（Egyptian spear）：早王朝時期以銅或青銅矛頭綁在木杆上的長兵器，經過數千年仍然留在第十八王朝的步兵編裝裡。埃及的矛頭多為扁平的柳葉形，帶中脊與尖鋌，裝在細長木杆前端，長度足以在成排盾牌的掩護下刺穿對手的胸腹；矛與短柄斧、月牙劍、匕首一同懸於步兵腰間，弓手則不持長兵。埃及遠征軍的火力骨幹是複合弓，箭袋裡備有數十支銅或骨製箭頭的箭，另有投擲棒這類可在近距離拋出的短兵器。車兵乘雙人戰車，一人御者一人射手，車上另備短矛與箭囊，馬匹由利比亞與敘利亞沿海征集，體型小而耐走。攻城方面備有斜坡、築起的土壘、木槌與撞角，工兵會先勘查水源，再決定是封堵還是壅塞。北方聯軍的裝備與之相近：青銅長矛、圓盾、複合弓與投石索，攻城則倚賴撞錘與塔車。整支遠征隊伍的補給靠尼羅河船運與陸路背囊並行，士兵自帶穀物、椰棗、葡萄酒與鹽，另有專門隊伍沿途徵收當地的穀物、銅料與馬匹。
kitsEn: The weapon on this card is the Egyptian spear: a long arm dating from the Early Dynastic period, with a copper or bronze head bound to a wooden shaft, still carried by the infantry of the Eighteenth Dynasty after several thousand years. Egyptian spearheads were usually flat and lanceolate in outline, with a central rib and a socket, fitted to the front of a slim wooden shaft long enough to pierce an opponent's chest and belly behind a rank of shields; the spear was hung at the infantryman's side together with the short-handled axe, the khopesh and the dagger, while the archers carried no long weapon at all. The firepower backbone of the Egyptian expeditionary force was the composite bow, with quivers holding dozens of arrows tipped with copper or bone, and there were also throwing sticks, short weapons that could be hurled at close range. The chariotry rode in two-man cars, a driver and an archer, with extra spears and a quiver carried on the car, and the horses were levied from Libya and the Syrian coast, small animals with a strong staying power. For siege work the Egyptians had ramps, raised embankments, wooden mauls and battering rams, and the engineers surveyed the water supply first before deciding whether to block it or dam it. The equipment of the northern coalition was similar: bronze spears, round shields, composite bows and slings, with rams and siege towers for assault. The supply of the whole expedition rested on Nile shipping and on pack trains moving in parallel along the land route, the soldiers carrying their own grain, dates, wine and salt, while separate units levied grain, copper and horses from the districts they passed through.
tactics: 埃及的遠征是一套有固定次序的軍事機器。行軍時以縱隊前進，前鋒是清除道路的先遣與弓手，主力步兵居中，車隊與衛兵隨後，最後是載著王室的車乘與隨軍祭司；各隊之間拉開距離，靠號角與旗幔維持聯絡。進入會戰地域後，埃及軍通常以步兵結成方陣或新月形的縱深，車兵分置兩翼或三面，等待弓手射擊與步兵接觸的時機；圖特摩斯三世在梅格多戰役浮雕上的箭雨壓制、縱隊前進與追擊潰軍，正是這套戰法的標準形象。遠征真正的難題是水：沙漠路段必須事先指定井站、蓄水池與行軍日程，一旦離開河谷，便靠每日定量配給維持。圍城時埃及的做法是合圍封路、切斷城中水源、抬高壘土逼近城牆，並以隨軍工匠修築攻城的斜坡；對方往往在城破之前送出求和書。北方聯軍的戰法偏重守勢與消耗：依托城垣、渡口與地勢，用游騎與遊牧部族襲擾埃及的給養線，使遠征隊在缺糧缺馬時不得不退兵；聯軍內部各懷心思，戰線一破便各自散去，這是這類戰爭中最常見的情形。
tacticsEn: The Egyptian expedition was a military machine working to a fixed order. On the march the army moved in column: at the front the advance guard clearing the road together with the archers, then the main body of infantry, then the chariots and the guard, and last of all the royal carriage with the army's priests; the units were spaced apart and kept in touch by trumpet calls and by standards. On reaching the ground of a pitched battle the Egyptians usually formed the infantry into a square or into a crescent in depth, with the chariots posted on two or three flanks, waiting for the moment when the archers had shot and the infantry had closed. The reliefs of the battle of Megiddo, with the rain of arrows, the advance of the columns and the pursuit of the broken enemy, are the standard image of that method. The real difficulty of the expedition was water: the stages across the desert had to be planned in advance with named wells, cisterns and a marching timetable, and once the army left the river valleys it subsisted on a fixed daily ration. When it came to siege, the Egyptians closed in, cut the roads, cut off the water supply of the town, raised earthworks against the walls and had the engineers who had come with the army build assault ramps; the defenders generally sent a request for terms before the breach. The tactics of the northern coalition leaned towards the defensive and towards wearing the enemy down: holding behind city walls, fords and favourable ground, sending out light horse and nomadic tribes to harry the Egyptian supply line so that the expedition would have to withdraw for want of food and horses. The coalition was itself divided, and once its line broke the contingents scattered, which was the commonest ending of wars of this kind.
data: 可用的數字集中在年代與編制兩端。圖特摩斯三世在位約公元前1479至前1425年，王曆二十一歲又兩個月；卡爾納克與孟斐斯的王室銘文列出他在位期間的敘利亞遠征，合計十七次以上，其中若干年裡一年出發兩三次，可見「第十四」只是編號而不是單一會戰。本站的戰爭列表把這場戰爭繫於公元前1440年，其錨點則是前1457年的梅格多之戰與前1453年的卡迭石之戰，那兩役之後埃及在黎凡特的體系才告成形。軍隊規模沒有直接記載，學界對第十八王朝遠征軍的常見估計是步兵數千人至上萬人，車兵數百乘，每乘兩人；後來的文件顯示官方的戰利品申報以頭、件、錠、匹為單位，數目常以數百、數千計，而不像後世史書那樣列出確切的傷亡數。疆域方面，埃及在這段時期的實際控制從比布魯斯、烏加里特等海港一路延伸到幼發拉底河上游的埃馬爾，縱深逾三百公里。地名上，卡迭石在今敘利亞北部奧龍特斯河東岸，約北緯34.9度、東經34.5度；圖尼普的位置仍有爭議，一般置於奧龍特斯河谷中段，卡特納則在霍姆斯西南。以上數字之外，這場戰役本身可核的記載有限。
dataEn: The usable numbers cluster around the chronology and the order of battle. Thutmose III reigned from about 1479 to 1425 BC, twenty-one regnal years and two months; the royal inscriptions at Karnak and Memphis list his Syrian campaigns, seventeen or more in all, and in several of those years he set out two or three times, so that the number fourteen is a label and not a single battle. The list of wars followed by this site dates the present war to 1440 BC, while its anchor points are the battle of Megiddo in 1457 BC and the battle of Kadesh in 1453 BC, after which the Egyptian system in the Levant took shape. There is no direct record of the size of the army; the usual scholarly estimate for an Eighteenth Dynasty expedition is infantry in the thousands up to some ten thousand, with several hundred chariots of two men each. Later documents show that official claims of spoil were reckoned in head, item, ingot and hide, and that the figures were commonly given in hundreds or thousands, and not as exact casualty lists in the manner of later historiography. As for territory, Egyptian control in this period ran from the ports of Byblos and Ugarit all the way to Emar on the upper Euphrates, a depth of more than three hundred kilometres. As for place names, Kadesh stands on the east bank of the Orontes in northern Syria, at roughly 34.9 degrees north and 34.5 degrees east; the site of Tunip is still disputed and is generally placed in the middle Orontes valley, while Qatna lies south-west of Homs. Beyond these figures, the record of this particular campaign is thin.
cause: 打起嚟的理由是三層的。最表層是地理：埃及要守住尼羅河與地中海之間的迦南走廊，必須把從比布魯斯到幼發拉底河渡口這條線上的城邦握在手裡，因為這條線同時是木材、銅料與馬匹進口的通道，也是通往小亞細亞的跳板。第二層是米坦尼的崛起：胡里人控制的米坦尼王國在幼發拉底河上游與敘利亞北端建立了據點，直接壓在埃及北界之上；兩強對卡迭石與圖尼普的爭奪，實質是誰來決定奧龍特斯河兩岸的稅關歸屬。第三層是附庸體系的鬆動：埃及的遠征每次都要求西敘利亞城邦納貢、派駐官吏，一旦北方盟主施加壓力，這些小邦就會兩面下注；卡迭石長期拒絕朝貢，圖尼普與卡特納在兩強之間搖擺，正是整個結構裡最脆弱的一環。於是每一季的遠征既是懲罰，也是重新確認宗主權的儀式，而維持這套儀式的成本年年累積，最終把雙方都拖進一場曠日持久的消耗。
causeEn: There were three layers of reason behind the fighting. The outermost was geography: Egypt had to hold the corridor of Canaan between the Nile and the sea, and to do so it had to keep in its hands the line of city-states running from Byblos to the crossings of the Euphrates, because that line was at once the channel for imported timber, copper and horses and the stepping-stone towards Anatolia. The second layer was the rise of Mitanni: the Hurrian-run kingdom of Mitanni had established itself on the upper Euphrates and in northern Syria, pressing directly on Egypt's northern frontier, and the contest between the two powers over Kadesh and Tunip was in truth a contest over who would collect the tolls on both banks of the Orontes. The third layer was the loosening of the system of vassals: every Egyptian expedition demanded tribute and installed officials in the city-states of western Syria, and as soon as the northern king applied pressure these small states began to play both sides; the long refusal of Kadesh to pay tribute and the wavering of Tunip and Qatna between the two powers marked the weakest joints of the whole structure. Each season's expedition was therefore both a punishment and a ceremony for the reaffirmation of suzerainty, and the cost of keeping up that ceremony accumulated year on year until it dragged both sides into a war of attrition.
impact: 從長遠看，這場戰爭的意義不在一時勝負，而在它把埃及的帝國體制固定下來。公元前14世紀的近東出現了一套成熟的朝貢秩序：附庸城邦按年進貢象牙、金銀、銅料、馬匹、酒、油與穀物，埃及回以「禮物」與恩惠；這套秩序後來被赫梯學去，又透過往返的書信被記錄下來，成為早期國際外交的樣板。另一層影響是權力平衡：米坦尼退守上美索不達米亞，赫梯在安納托利亞東端坐大，敘利亞變成三方爭奪的棋盤；埃及不再是唯一的霸主，卻仍握有海路與南方的資源，得以一代代維持遠征。戰術層面上，這類年年出征的消耗戰逼出了遠征軍的後勤技術——井站與定量配給、尼羅河船運、海路與陸路並行補給——這些做法後來被其他遠征的將領沿用。對文字材料的意義同樣不小：這段時期留下的王室銘文、書吏日誌與後來的書信，是我們重建當時戰爭的主要依據，也是理解青銅時期晚期國際秩序的少數原始材料。
impactEn: In the long run the significance of this war lay not in any single success or failure but in the fact that it fixed the Egyptian imperial system in place. In the fourteenth century BC the Near East produced a mature tribute order: the vassal city-states paid yearly tribute in ivory, gold and silver, copper, horses, wine, oil and grain, and Egypt answered with gifts and bounty; the order was later taken up by Hatti and recorded in the exchange of letters, and it became the model for early international diplomacy. A second effect was on the balance of power: Mitanni fell back on upper Mesopotamia, Hatti grew strong in eastern Anatolia, and Syria became a chessboard contested by three powers. Egypt was no longer the sole hegemon, yet it still held the sea route and the resources of the south, and so could keep up its expeditions generation after generation. On the tactical level, a war of this kind, fought out year after year, forced out the logistical techniques of the expeditionary army: designated wells and daily rations, transport by the Nile, supply by sea and by land in parallel. These practices were later taken over by commanders on other campaigns. The significance for the written record is just as great: the royal inscriptions, the clerks' journals and the later letters of this period are the principal evidence for reconstructing the wars of the time, and among the few surviving original sources for the international order of the Late Bronze Age.
result: 結果是沒有決定性會戰，只有不斷加深的附庸關係。埃及在這場戰爭中沒有攻下一座足以改變地圖的大城，卡迭石仍在卡迭石王手中，聯軍的聯盟也沒有被徹底瓦解；取而代之的是一季又一季的遠征，敵方每一次被打服、繳械、求和，再在幾年之後重新挑釁。遠征的實際成果表現在幾個方面：西敘利亞諸邦再次確認向埃及朝貢，圖尼普與卡特納的使者帶著貢物來到孟斐斯與卡爾納克，埃馬爾與烏加里特在保持獨立的同時繳納銀與銅；埃及的北方邊界從此固定在奧龍特斯河與幼發拉底河上游一帶，北部的小亞細亞與愛琴海世界也透過烏加里特連成一線。放到更長的時間軸上看，這條向北的通道最終被另一條路徑取代：幾十年後埃及與赫梯議和，前1370年簽訂的卡迭石和約是已知最早的一紙國際條約；再往後，拉美西斯二世與赫梯在卡迭石再戰，卡迭石詩篇描繪十三位盟王聯手，說明這段走廊始終是列強必爭之地。就前1440年這一次遠征而言，可以確定的是：埃及既沒有崩潰也沒有大幅擴張，它只是把一套帝國的骨架釘在黎凡特，而當年那些長矛、複合弓與雙人戰車，就是這套骨架最實在的部分。
resultEn: The result was no decisive battle, only a deepening of the relationship of dependence. Egypt took in this war no city large enough to redraw the map, Kadesh remained in the hands of the king of Kadesh, and the coalition was not broken apart for good; in place of a settlement came expedition after expedition, the enemy beaten, disarmed and suing for terms, then challenging again a few years later. The practical results of the expeditions showed themselves in several ways: the city-states of western Syria once more confirmed their tribute to Egypt, envoys from Tunip and Qatna came to Memphis and Karnak with their deliveries, and Emar and Ugarit, while keeping their independence, paid in silver and copper; Egypt's northern frontier was henceforth fixed along the Orontes and the upper Euphrates, and the world of northern Anatolia and the Aegean was linked into the same line through Ugarit. On a longer axis, this northern corridor was eventually replaced by another route: a few decades later Egypt and Hatti made peace, and the treaty of Kadesh concluded in 1370 BC is the earliest surviving international treaty known to us; later still, Ramesses II fought Hatti again at Kadesh, and the Poem of Kadesh describes thirteen allied kings acting together, showing that this corridor remained a prize for every power. As for the expedition of 1440 BC itself, what can be certain is this: Egypt neither collapsed nor expanded greatly; it simply nailed the frame of an empire to the Levant, and the spears, composite bows and two-man chariots of those years were the most solid part of that frame.
